title: Broker audit record
description: One outcome of one broker operation, written by the broker service as its own file (homelabnext.broker.state). Every call, submit, status, run, cancel, approve and deny leaves exactly one record, whatever the outcome: ok, denied (refused by policy, ownership, approval or a lane), invalid (malformed arguments or a request in the wrong state), error (the handler failed or timed out) or shadow (decided, not run). reason is empty for ok and required otherwise. args are the request's arguments with every argument its spec marks secret replaced by <redacted> and every value over 1 KiB replaced by its size and digest; secrets passed to handlers by name never appear. 1.1 adds, additively, the operation connect (a refusal by the socket transport before an operation could be attributed: an unknown peer, an actor named in the body, an oversized or malformed request) and via (the authenticated transport peer that carried the request, uid:<n>). 1.2 adds, additively, the outcome started: the intent record a call or run writes before its action executes (the broker writes it with an empty reason). The broker refuses to execute when it cannot be written, so every action that ran has one; its ok, denied or error record completes it, and a started record with none means the outcome could not be recorded (a full disk) or the process died while the action ran. 1.3 adds, additively, Code Mode capability tokens (ADR-0031): the operations token-issue (a runner asking for a token for an in-flight codemode.execute request) and token-spend (a token ended, by its runner or by the end of its codemode.execute), and token_id and execution_id, which every record of a call or submit made with a token carries, refusals of the token included (a secret that names no token has neither). The token's secret is never recorded.

caller.description: Who asked, as presented (a profile id, a caller name, or issuer:subject for an approver).

action.description: The action named; empty when an unknown request id was named.

reason.description: Machine reason: a decision reason (schemas/broker/decision), not-request-owner, or a lane or handler reason (lane-path-escape, handler-digest-mismatch, ...).

decision_reason.description: On an ok submit: the decision behind it (allowed, approval-required).

request_id.description: The request acted on, as presented (a refused id is recorded verbatim).

token_id.description: 1.3: the Code Mode capability token the call was made with, or the one issued or spent.

execution_id.description: 1.3: the Code Mode execution that token belongs to.

via.description: The authenticated socket peer that carried the request (absent for in-process and CLI calls).
